newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy stake in STET/Telecom to fall below 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy stake in STET/Telecom to fall below 50 pct.

text.p: The Italian government's stake in the merged STET/Telecom Italia grouping will fall below 50 percent, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday.

He was speaking to the transport and telecommunications commission of parliament on the state's holding when the two groups are merged, but he did not give a precise figure for the state's holding in the combined STET/Telecom grouping.
"After the merger the stake will fall to below 50 percent, but I don't know the exact number," Ciampi said.
Currently, the Italian Treasury has a controlled stake in STET which in turn has a majority stake in Telecom Italia. After merger the government plans to privatise the combined group.

Ciampi said that the government favoured keeping a golden share in STET. This came after a constitutional court in late January allowed a proposed referendum seeking to abolish the use of golden shares, which give the Treasury special powers in privatised companies deemed to be of public interest.
He added that there will be a referendum on the golden share issue, and the government will acknowledge the decision if the vote is to abolish golden shares.
Ciampi also confirmed that STET would be looking to sell-off its interests in Italtel and cable laying group Sirti .
